description: Pill showing a role or tag name. With a color, the background is a 15% tint of that color and a matching dot precedes the label; the dot is aria-hidden, so the color is decoration and the name carries the meaning. With onRemove, a small remove button follows the label.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the remove button, when there is one. The chip itself is not focusable.

focus.notes: The remove button uses the browser's default focus outline (no custom ring). When removeDisabled is set it is disabled and leaves the tab order.

announcements: Reads the name as plain text.
The remove button announces as "Remove <name>" (or removeAriaLabel).
screenReader.notes: Don't rely on the color alone to distinguish roles: the name must be meaningful on its own.

contrast.text: text-foreground on a 15% tint of the chosen color over the page background; keep the color mid-to-dark so the tint stays light. Without a color, text-muted-foreground on bg-muted.
contrast.ui: The remove icon is drawn at 60% opacity; it passes 3:1 on light tints but check it on saturated colors.

motion.reducedMotion: Only a color/opacity transition on hover.

consumerResponsibilities: Pass removeAriaLabel when "Remove <name>" isn't the right wording or language.
Move focus somewhere sensible after a chip is removed (for example to the next chip or the input that adds chips).
The remove button is 14px; give it room or a larger hit area in dense lists (WCAG 2.5.8 target size).
